note: Theming-only module: registers a block_content theme hook backed by templates/block-content.html.twig, forces custom blocks to use it via hook_block_content_view_alter, and adds a suggestion cascade (block_content__<view_mode|bundle|bundle__view_mode|id|id__view_mode>). No config/routes/permissions. Medium cases create a real custom block-content type (bundle) on the live site and require the agent to read that bundle and apply the module's documented template-suggestion naming. Hard cases require the module installed so custom blocks render through its template (reset uninstalls; verify checks the module is installed and its template file is present). NOTE: this site's theme.registry->get() currently throws due to an unrelated contrib module, so scripts intentionally avoid it and use moduleExists + template-file checks instead.

evals.prompt: What does the block_content_template module add to Drupal, and what is the name of the Twig template file it provides for custom block content entities?
evals.expected_output: It registers a block_content theme hook backed by templates/block-content.html.twig and makes every rendered custom (content) block use it, so custom blocks can be themed like other entities.

evals.prompt: Using block_content_template, how would I create a Twig template that only themes custom blocks of a specific block type (bundle)? What naming does its theme-suggestion scheme use?
evals.expected_output: The module adds theme suggestions block_content__<view_mode>, block_content__<bundle>, block_content__<bundle>__<view_mode>, block_content__<id>, block_content__<id>__<view_mode>. For a bundle-specific template add block-content--<bundle>.html.twig to your theme.

evals.prompt: Which variables and CSS classes does block_content_template make available when rendering a custom block through its template?
evals.expected_output: Variables id, bundle, view_mode, label and content are available. The default template outputs classes block-content, block-content--type-<bundle>, block-content--<id>, block-content--view-mode-<view_mode> and wraps fields in a block-content__content div.

evals.prompt: A custom block content type has been added to this site for theming. Inspect the site to find its machine name, then, using block_content_template's suggestion scheme, give the Twig template filename you would add to your theme to override ONLY that block type's markup.
evals.expected_output: The custom block type is bct_probe. Its bundle-specific suggestion is block_content__bct_probe, so add block-content--bct-probe.html.twig to your theme.

evals.prompt: This site has a custom block content type added for theming. Inspect the site for its machine name, then give the block_content_template Twig template filename that would override that block type's markup specifically in the 'full' view mode.
evals.expected_output: The block type is bct_probe. The bundle+view-mode suggestion is block_content__bct_probe__full, so the template is block-content--bct-probe--full.html.twig.

evals.prompt: Custom (content) block entities on this site should render through block_content_template's block-content.html.twig so they can be themed per bundle. Ensure the block_content_template module is installed on the site.
evals.expected_output: block_content_template is installed (drush en block_content_template); it registers the block_content theme hook backed by its templates/block-content.html.twig so custom blocks render through the template.

evals.prompt: I want to be able to give my reusable custom blocks their own template file in my theme, the way pages and articles have templates. Please turn on whatever is needed so my custom blocks get their own template.
evals.expected_output: Enabling block_content_template gives custom block entities their own block-content.html.twig template and per-bundle/per-view-mode theme suggestions; the module is installed and its template file is present.
